headline: Official Recreation and Spring Entry Reservations
reservation: High-demand springs like Alexander and Silver Glen require individual day-use fees; capacity is strictly limited and sites close when full. Juniper Run canoe launches require advanced booking through the official concessionaire, especially on weekends. Overnight stays at Salt Springs or Juniper Springs campgrounds should be secured months ahead through Recreation.gov, noting that entry and lodging are managed via separate systems.

days.title: Artesian Springs and Ancient Middens

stops.name: Silver Glen Springs Recreation Area
stops.detail: Swim in crystal-clear turquoise pools and observe the massive shell middens left by indigenous peoples.

stops.name: Alexander Springs
stops.detail: Explore the gently sloping spring basin for snorkeling or the only forest location for authorized scuba diving.

days.driving: Allow 60 to 90 minutes for forest road transitions; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: Springs often reach capacity by mid-morning during weekends or warm spells.

days.title: Paddling the Juniper Wilderness

stops.name: Juniper Run
stops.detail: Navigate a technical 7-mile canoe trail through a dense, winding canopy of palms and oaks.

stops.name: Juniper Springs Nature Trail
stops.detail: Walk the accessible boardwalks to see the historic mill house and resident wildlife.

days.driving: Local shuttle transfers are required for one-way paddles; allow 4-5 hours for the water route.
days.note: The Juniper Run is a narrow, technical paddle; ensure skill levels match the winding turns.

days.title: Historic Trails and Scrub Habitats

stops.name: Yearling Trail
stops.detail: Hike past historic sinkholes and 19th-century homestead remains inspired by classic Florida literature.

stops.name: Florida Black Bear Scenic Byway
stops.detail: Drive through the Big Scrub, the largest contiguous patch of sand pine scrub in the world.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for scenic loops and trail access; unpaved sections require caution.
days.note: Sand pine scrub offers little shade; carry significant water and sun protection.

intel.title: Spring Capacity
intel.text: Major springs use a 'one-in, one-out' policy once capacity is reached. Arrive at gated entrances before 9 AM during peak season to avoid being turned away.

intel.title: Forest Gateways
intel.text: Refuel in Silver Springs or Eustis before entering the deep forest interior. Service stations are sparse once you depart the main state roads.

intel.title: Seasonal Wildlife
intel.text: Visit Salt Springs Run between November and March for the highest probability of manatee sightings. Manatee presence depends on water temperature shifts.

intel.title: Trailhead Safety
intel.text: Use designated parking areas at the Yearling Trail and Florida Trail crossings. Avoid parking on soft sandy shoulders where vehicles can easily become stuck.

intel.title: Offline Navigation
intel.text: Cellular reception is unreliable within the Juniper Prairie Wilderness and deep scrub areas. Download maps for offline use before departing Ocala or Daytona Beach.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at DAB and secure groceries in Ocala or Silver Springs before checking into forest-adjacent lodging.
plan.vehicle: An SUV is recommended for unpaved forest service roads; check rental agreements for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Florida Black Bear Scenic Byway pullouts for sunset; visibility varies with humidity.
